title: Lyon 2021 §6 T-junction extension into conforming quad layout
description: Lyon 2021 §6 first paragraph: from a quantized T-mesh, iteratively extend each T-junction across its incident patch to the opposite side. If the quantization on the opposite side has a node at the matching parametric distance, connect to it; otherwise split the opposing arc to create one. Loop until no T-junctions remain. Output is the conforming quad layout: every patch is a 4-sided quad bounded by separatrices that align (within α) with the seamless parametrization's iso-lines. THIS IS THE PAPER'S DELIVERABLE — every entry in Lyon Table 1 (#P column) is a count of these conforming patches. Note: this is independent of whether dense interior quads are emitted; the layout is the algorithm output, the dense quads are 'for visualization purposes' (§6 ¶2) using LCBK19 harmonic quad grids (separate ticket PATCH-75).
definition-of-done: New QuadLayout class: List<QuadLayoutPatch> patches, each with 4 ordered side polylines (sequences of layout-arc IDs) and 4 corner node IDs. Built by extending T-junctions per §6. Verification: on Hand-30k with synthetic q≡1, output should have all 4-sided patches (no T-junctions). On any real-mesh quantization, every patch must be 4-sided (assertion). Patch count #P recorded for Table 1 comparison.
testing-plan: Toy: 2x2 T-mesh with one explicit T-junction, verify it gets resolved to a conforming 4-quad layout. Hand-30k: assert all output patches 4-sided, count matches T-mesh patch count + (#T-junctions - resolved). ROCKERARM-style fixture (deferred until cross-field stage runs on it): expect #P in 100-200 range.
